You do not normally need this file. Run ./scripts/dev-setup.sh instead: it
generates a database password, stores it in the .NET user-secrets store, and
writes the .env file that Docker Compose reads. The user-secrets store is
outside the repository, so the password cannot be committed.
To set the connection string by hand instead:
dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:YuruChara" \
"Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=yuruchara;Username=yuruchara;Password=<password>" \
--project src/YuruChara.Api
YuruChara.Api and YuruChara.Ingestion declare the same UserSecretsId, so that
one command configures both, and the EF Core tooling reads the same store.
Run ./scripts/dev-setup.sh afterwards to rewrite .env from the new value.
This file exists for the case where a local JSON file is preferred over the
secret store: copy it to appsettings.Development.json and fill in the value.
That file is excluded by .gitignore. The secret store is still the better
choice, because a file inside the working tree can still be committed with
`git add -f`, included in a directory copy, or picked up by a backup tool.
In CI or a deployed environment, set the ConnectionStrings__YuruChara
environment variable. The double underscore is how ASP.NET Core maps a flat
variable name onto the nested ConnectionStrings:YuruChara configuration key.
